metadata.title: Threat Detection SSPP
metadata.remarks: This SSPP defines how monitored security telemetry is analyzed and evaluated to determine whether observed behavior constitutes suspected malicious activity requiring escalation.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits authority, workflow, escalation, telemetry, and monitoring requirements and SHALL NOT redefine those concerns.

system-characteristics.system-description: Defines analytic, confidence, and escalation requirements for determining whether observed activity is suspicious or malicious.

system-implementation.remarks: Threat Detection evaluates observed behavior and produces determinations. It SHALL NOT initiate response actions, modify systems, or bypass escalation pathways.

detection-scope.description: Suspicious or malicious identity usage, authentication anomalies, or privilege misuse.
Suspicious or malicious process, service, or host behavior.
Suspicious or malicious communication patterns or lateral movement indicators.
Suspicious or malicious application and API behavior.

detection-requirements.statement: Detections SHALL include a confidence assessment based on available evidence.
Detections SHALL identify affected assets, identities, and timeframes.
Detections SHALL reference monitoring context and supporting telemetry.
Detection logic SHALL be repeatable and reviewable.

confidence-handling.description: Low-confidence detections SHALL remain advisory and SHALL NOT escalate automatically.
Medium-confidence detections SHALL trigger analyst review.
High-confidence detections SHALL escalate to Incident Response in accordance with workflow rules.

control-implementation.description: Controls ensure threat determinations are accurate, attributable, and escalated appropriately.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Analytic mechanisms are employed to identify potential malicious activity.
Confirmed detections are escalated to incident handling according to defined criteria.

statements.statement: Threat Detection SHALL NOT execute response, containment, or remediation actions.
Automation SHALL NOT independently declare incidents or suppress escalation.
Uncertain or incomplete telemetry SHALL reduce confidence, not be ignored.
Detection logic SHALL be subject to review and governance oversight.

back-matter.remarks: Downstream SSPPs for Incident Response, SOAR, and Digital Forensics SHALL treat detections produced under this SSPP as advisory inputs requiring explicit authorization and workflow transition.
